headline: Learned models encode fragment topology and bond-edit search for molecular structure
label: Learned Models Of Molecular Interactions
summary: Recent preprints couple topology-aware molecular languages and graph-edit search to fragment editing and structure elucidation, alongside security analysis of…
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models that operate on explicit molecular structure rather than flat sequence or fingerprint inputs. STAMP encodes fragment motifs, attachment sites and tree topology in a molecular language to support fragment-level learning and editing. GEMS treats structure elucidation as learned search over isomer graphs, applying 2-switch bond edits scored by MIST fingerprint predictions, and reports improved Hit@1 for metabolomics structure elucidation. What is new here is the pairing of topology-aware representation with graph-edit search for structure-level tasks. A third preprint, on data poisoning of protein language models (ProtGPT2, ProGen2) and of a retrieval corpus for a text-guided protein generator, addresses the security of training and retrieval pipelines rather than structure modeling. Because the items differ in task and benchmark, their reported results are not directly comparable.
